pull.title: fix(review): make each handled outside-diff bullet name its finding, and re-check the PR right before land-pr merges
pull.body:
PRs #178, #180, #191 and #193 merged with CodeRabbit findings nobody had read. Main now counts outside-diff findings, but filler bullets still passed that count, and land-pr merged with no second look after READY. This PR makes each handled bullet name its finding, and re-checks the PR just before the merge.

## What changed

- **Gate A, review-status.mjs:** an outside-diff finding counts as handled only when a bullet in "Outside-diff: handled" names its 24-hex CodeRabbit marker id (whole token) or its path:lines. Findings are collected across every CodeRabbit review body, each id once. A body with no markers falls back to the count, so a format change fails closed. Nitpicks need no bullet.
- **Gate C, land-recheck.mjs and land-pr.ps1:** right before the merge, land-pr refuses when:
  - the head moved;
  - a CodeRabbit review or summary edit is newer than the READY check;
  - a review request is unanswered (a trusted summary that covers the head is an answer, as on #211);
  - the CodeRabbit status is pending.
  READY time is taken 120 s early, so clock skew fails closed. Read errors refuse. `-IgnoreReview` still bypasses. `land-recheck.mjs` joins `checkpoint.critical`.
- **Deferred from #225 round 3:** the rate-limit line no longer asks for a second review after a paid one. `cr-paid` numbers rounds correctly. Rule text: filtered files are not reviewed, but billing exclusion is unproven.
- **Docs:** `pr-review-loop.md` describes both gates. The proposal records Dave's D-2 hold.

## Evidence

Proof type: bugfix

RED: `node --test scripts/github/review-status.test.mjs scripts/github/cr-paid.test.mjs scripts/github/land-recheck.test.mjs` @ 66a3b385
```text
(this branch's test files run against main's sources at 66a3b385)
review-status + cr-paid: tests 281, pass 268, fail 13
not ok 273 - ID-A: filler bullets do not handle live PR 221 findings
not ok 16 - CP15: two review objects on two commits label the next round 3, and the fix limits still apply
not ok 2 - scripts\github\land-recheck.test.mjs (land-recheck.mjs does not exist on main)
```

GREEN: `node --test scripts/github/*.test.mjs scripts/mods/validate-mods.test.mjs scripts/rules/test/coderabbit-cli-content.test.mjs` @ 83679590
```text
node --test: tests 683, pass 683, fail 0
pwsh scripts/github/land-pr-recheck.test.ps1: passed=14 failed=0
claude plugin test .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods: 1025 pass, 0 fail
npx vitest run (.claude/hooks): 109 files, 2916 passed
context-budget-guard 23512/23516; ondemand-index-check OK; rule-router probe 139/139; review-skip-sync OK
e2e replay review-status.mjs --json: #178 2, #180 2, #191 1, #193 4 unnamed outside-diff findings listed by id and path:lines; #221 and #225 no new false block
e2e land-recheck.mjs on #205 #211 #213 #217 #221 #225: unchanged since the READY check, exit 0
```

Artifacts: `.claude/cache/e2e/2026-10-30-mergegate-red.txt`.

## Reviews before this PR opened

- Investigation agent: all four merges passed READY; the unread findings were outside-diff only. Main's count gate (67c65adf, #225) already blocks all four.
- Opus review of the build: 1 Major (gate C refused every clean summary-only round, #211 shape) and 5 Minors (clock skew, short marker ids, stale text, a duplicated user check, header wording). All fixed. A follow-up fix makes gate C trust a summary only through its edit history, like READY.
- pre-pr CodeRabbit CLI on 72c96eb2: 2 Minors (a timing-dependent test bound, a long rule sentence), fixed in a5dc61d1.

## CodeRabbit round 1 (a5dc61d1, paid $3.00 by policy)

3 Minors (status read not paginated, fail-open; no retry after a paid post that never ran; summary round miscount), fixed test-first in e038f042.

## CodeRabbit round 2 (e038f042, free slot)

1 Major (the paid gate's wait and retry branches could overlap), fixed test-first in 83679590.

CLI fix review: e038f04..8367959 clean

## Scope not included

- Nitpick findings need no handled bullet.
- Option B and D-2 (PR-Agent pilot): on hold (Dave).

Model + harness: claude-opus-5-5 (orchestration, Opus review) and Sonnet kraken agents via Claude Code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_0162xu8GPKraAf3vEmY7PuV8

## Summary by CodeRabbit

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Pull requests are rechecked immediately before merging. A changed commit, newer review activity, an unresolved review request, a pending CodeRabbit status, or unavailable check data can prevent the merge.
  * Outside-diff findings are tracked by unique markers or exact file locations, so each finding must be identified before review is considered complete.
  * Paid-review guidance clarifies when to wait for a review or request a follow-up. Estimated review rounds now reflect distinct commits covered by prior reviews.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for merge checks, review tracking, and paid-review instructions.

app.description:
# 🦉 What is GitGuardian?

GitGuardian Secrets Detection detects and fixes vulnerabilities in source code at every step of the software development lifecycle, covering 350+ types of secrets like API keys, database connection strings, private keys, certificates, and more. The platform’s policy engine enables security teams to monitor and enforce rules across their VCS, DevOps tools, and infrastructure-as-code configurations. Our automated remediation playbooks and collaboration features bring security and development teams together to resolve incidents fast and in full.

## 1. Scan your codebase for 350+ types of secrets
GitGuardian scans your GitHub repositories and raises alerts only for critical secrets, such as API keys or other credentials. At scale, GitGuardian’s detection algorithm has been battle-tested on over three years of activity in all public GitHub repositories – totaling over 1 billion scanned commits!

## 2. Quickly remediate your hard-coded secrets
If you ever experience a leak involving a credential, we have a complete remediation guide used by 100k+ developers each year. We’ll show you how to revoke the secret and remove it from your git history.

##  3. Prevent secrets from reaching GitHub
Install ggshield, the GitGuardian CLI, and add secrets detection to your local development workflow using pre-commit and pre-push git hooks integrations.

# 🙋‍♂️ FAQ

**What is your pricing?**
GitGuardian is free for teams under 25 developers and offers a 30-day trial for larger teams.

**How can I be sure that GitGuardian won’t raise too many false positives?**
We have scanned billions of commits, sent millions of alerts since 2018, and integrated each feedback to improve our algorithm. Our alerts currently receive 91% “true positive” feedback from developers.

**My repositories are private; why should I install automated secret detection?**
Imagine if there were a plain text file with all your credit card numbers inside, you wouldn’t put this file inside your company’s git repository. Secrets are just as sensitive and should be handled with special care.

**Is GitGuardian available to be installed on-premise?**
Yes, you can contact one of our security specialists to look over the possibility of installing GitGuardian on-premise on your repositories.

# ⚒️ Installation notes 

You should install GitGuardian directly through your [GitGuardian](https://dashboard.gitguardian.com/) workspace on the Integration settings page. 

So that you know, your GitHub organization or GitHub account can only be associated with a single GitGuardian workspace.

# 👋 Support

If you experience any difficulties or have any questions, please reach out to us by email ([support@gitguardian.com](mailto:support@gitguardian.com)).

commit.message:
fix(land-recheck): read every commit-status page, retry a paid review that never came, count summary rounds

CodeRabbit #227 round 1 (3 Minor). land-recheck read one status page, so a pending CodeRabbit status past 30 statuses was missed (fail-open); it now pages. The rate-limit line no longer drops the included-review fallback after a paid post: if no review appears within 30 minutes, check capacity and post once. cr-paid counts an earlier summary-only round before a later review object. Tests RC10f, CW4n2, CP17 were RED, now GREEN.

_doc: classes: path globs per risk class. Only ** (any number of whole path segments, also zero), * (inside one segment) and ? are special.

A glob that starts with ! is an exclusion for that class (r3 excludes eval fixtures under .claude/skills/**/evals/**). Each path gets the first class that matches it, in this order: r3, infra, steering, docs.
A path that matches no class is normal. The PR class is the highest class of any path. risk:high is never set from paths: a person adds it.
deep_enabled false: steering, infra, high and r3 PRs get review:coderabbit + review:deep-held, not review:deep (spec 4.1, Apex billing D3).
greptile.credits_used_manual: Greptile credits used this period, an integer you edit by hand. null means unknown: the router skips the u1 and u2 steps and the ledger says so.
greptile.u1_used: at or above this count, a review:deep PR gets a warning in the router comment.
greptile.u2_used: at or above this count, only r3 PRs get review:deep. Other deep classes get the held labels. Needs deep_enabled true.

greptile.u3_date: on or after this date, a deep-class PR gets one credit-check line in the router comment, but only while credits_used_manual is null. A known count means the check is done, so no line.
greptile.notify_login: GitHub login named in the u1 and u3 lines. null means nobody is pinged.
budget: CodeRabbit PR reviews per class as [opening, extra after a Major] (pr-review-loop.md 'PR review budget per class'). Read by scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.mjs. A bare number is [n, 0].

checkpoint.critical: path globs of files whose PR gets Greptile too when it is available (pr-checkpoint.mjs rule R3). A PR that touches one never takes the READY carry (review-status.mjs). Extended 2026-10-30 with the files where a fix added a real Major (.claudedocs/2026-10-30-coderabbit-rereview-study.md section 4).
checkpoint.parser: path globs of hand-written lexer and parser guards. Their PR gets one CodeRabbit review and no loop (rule R2). Dave edits this list.

checkpoint.enforce: boolean, read by the pre-pr-gate hook from the checkout the session runs in. true (live since PR D, 2026-10-29): the checkpoint rules (non-draft create, shell gh pr ready, hand review: label, self-confirm, non-literal --repo) deny the command. false (warn mode): the same commands pass and log one warn row to guard-decisions.jsonl. Only a literal true enforces. The stamp rules are enforced in both modes.

coderabbit.reviews_7d_manual: CodeRabbit PR reviews in the last 7 days, an integer Dave sets from the free '@coderabbitai rate limit' reply or the dashboard CSV export. null means unknown and changes no rule. reviews_7d_manual_date: the day Dave read it. A count older than 7 days counts as unknown.
